g2-implement.title: Crew launcher: pure role x harness model-tier resolver
g2-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md: add `ROLE_MODEL_TIERS: dict[str, dict[str, dict[str, object]]]` to scripts/run_crew.py, keyed harness -> role -> {"default": str, "allowed": frozenset[str]}, populated ONLY for harness "claude": admiral {default opus, allowed {opus}}; commander, implementer, reviewer, critic, cartographer {default sonnet, allowed {sonnet, haiku}}. Add harness keys "codex" and "local" as empty dicts -- the shape must express them, do not invent model identifiers for either (no codex/local dispatch exists anywhere in this repo). Add a small `ResolvedModel` dataclass (model: str, reason: str | None) and a pure, zero-I/O `resolve_model(role: str, harness: str, requested: str | None, reason: str | None) -> ResolvedModel` living beside build_crew_argv. Branches: (role, harness) absent from the table -> CrewLaunchError naming both the role and the harness (refuse, do not guess -- this is what makes an unpopulated codex/local dispatch refuse rather than invent); requested falsy -> ResolvedModel(default, None), no reason needed; requested given and not in allowed -> CrewLaunchError naming the requested model, the role, and the full allowed set (mirror the duplicate-crew-guard's named-refusal phrasing house style); requested in allowed but != default and reason falsy -> CrewLaunchError naming the model, the default it overrides, and that --reason is required; requested in allowed and (== default or reason given) -> ResolvedModel(requested, reason). Do NOT wire this into CrewLaunchSpec or build_parser yet -- this gate adds tested, unreferenced code only, so the full existing suite stays green untouched. Write a full unit-test class exercising every branch by direct import/call, zero subprocess/filesystem/argv. Dispatch a subagent invoking constellation-implementer. Wait for and integrate IMPLEMENTER_RESULT: `attach g2-implement --type implementer-result --field status=complete`.

g3-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md: add `reason: str | None = None` field to CrewLaunchSpec and `--reason` to build_parser() (plain optional flag). In CrewLaunchSpec.__post_init__, REPLACE the existing `if not self.model: raise CrewLaunchError(...)` block with a call to resolve_model(role=self.role, harness=self.launcher, requested=self.model, reason=self.reason), then set self.model/self.reason from the returned ResolvedModel (check whether CrewLaunchSpec is a frozen dataclass; if frozen, use object.__setattr__ for the two field writes, if not, plain assignment) -- this is the ONLY choke point, so this single edit automatically covers every CrewLaunchSpec construction site in the file (main()'s fresh-launch and abandon+relaunch paths, AND the launch_crew()/record_external_attempt() public wrapper functions -- confirmed by the plan critic that neither of those two is called from main() but both build a CrewLaunchSpec directly and must not bypass resolution). resume_crew() is UNTOUCHED -- it replays an already-resolved model/reason verbatim from a prior registry entry, never re-resolves, never requires --model/--reason (preserves existing resume behavior for legacy entries with no reason key). Thread spec.reason into build_entry() at both call sites (~1553, ~1708 in the pre-change file) as a new keyword; in build_entry, add `if reason: entry["reason"] = reason` beside the existing `if model: entry["model"] = model` line (same 'recorded when present' shape). Thread args.reason into main()'s CrewLaunchSpec construction. Update CrewLaunchSpec's docstring/error text so it no longer claims 'no default is invented' unconditionally -- name that a role/harness WITH a table entry now resolves a default, and only an undeclared role/harness or an out-of-set/unreasoned choice refuses. Rewrite the two existing tests that currently assert a no-model dispatch is refused for a POPULATED role (grep MandatoryModelTests for both the fresh-dispatch and the abandon-relaunch cases) to instead assert resolved-default behavior; add tests for: out-of-set model refused by name, unpopulated harness/role (e.g. launcher="codex") refused by name, non-default in-set model with no --reason refused, non-default in-set model WITH --reason recorded in the registry entry beside model, default-tier dispatch never requires/records a reason.
